transcript.text: Production Possibilities Frontier (PPF)
GENERAL ECONOMICS
GEN-ECON-08
Time: 5 minutes
Outcome: Interpret PPF points, slopes, shifts, efficiency, growth, and opportunity cost.
Difficulty: Beginner
THE CORE IDEA

A production possibilities frontier shows the combinations of two goods an economy can produce with its current resources and technology. A bowed-out PPF shows increasing opportunity cost: specialized resources become less well suited as production shifts toward the other good. Points inside indicate unused capacity; points outside are currently infeasible.
HOW TO RECOGNIZE IT
A PPF shows possible production combinations given current resources and technology.
A new technology improves only medical production.
An economy first removes unemployment, then gains new machinery.
Using idle resources changes the production point; resources or technology shift the frontier.
WATCH OUT

Do not confuse a PPF with a market curve. A PPF shows possible production combinations given current resources and technology. Using idle resources changes the production point; resources or technology shift the frontier.
WORKED EXAMPLE: READING A PPF

The horizontal axis is Good X and the vertical axis is Good Y. A bowed-out frontier passes through A at (0, 50), B at (8, 45), C at (15, 35), D at (21, 20), and E at (25, 0). F is inside the frontier near (8, 20), and G is outside it near (21, 48).

On the PPF, moving from point C (15 units of X and 35 of Y) to point D (21 of X and 20 of Y) gains 6 units of X but gives up 15 units of Y. The total opportunity cost is 15 units of Y, or 15/6 = 2.5 units of Y per additional unit of X.
CHECK YOURSELF
Does moving along a PPF represent economic growth?

Shortages and Surpluses
GENERAL ECONOMICS
GEN-ECON-17
Time: 5 minutes
Outcome: Determine equilibrium, shortages, surpluses, adjustment, and comparative statics.
Difficulty: Beginner
THE CORE IDEA

A shortage occurs when quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied at the current price. Buyers competing for limited supply put upward pressure on price. A surplus occurs when quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded; sellers then face pressure to lower price. Adjustment tends toward the price where the two quantities are equal.
HOW TO RECOGNIZE IT
At the current price, buyers want 180 units and sellers offer 120 units.
A price above equilibrium creates a surplus because quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded.
A price below equilibrium creates a shortage because quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied.
A surplus exists when quantity supplied is greater than quantity demanded.
WATCH OUT
A common mistake is to reverse shortage and price pressure. Quantity demanded exceeds quantity supplied, so there is a shortage. Shortages push price upward.
WORKED EXAMPLE: MEASURING A SHORTAGE

The horizontal axis is quantity of gas in thousands of gallons and the vertical axis is price of gas per gallon. D0 slopes downward from price $6 at quantity 0 to quantity 300 thousand at price $0. S0 slopes upward from the origin to price $6 at quantity 300 thousand. The curves intersect at price $3 and quantity 150 thousand. At price $2, quantity demanded is 200 thousand and quantity supplied is 100 thousand. At price $4, quantity demanded is 100 thousand and quantity supplied is 200 thousand.

At a price of $2 per gallon, the graph shows quantity demanded of 200 thousand gallons and quantity supplied of 100 thousand. Because buyers want 100 thousand more gallons than sellers offer, the market has a shortage of 200 - 100 = 100 thousand gallons. Upward pressure on price follows.
CHECK YOURSELF
At a price of $4, buyers want 100 thousand gallons and sellers offer 200 thousand. Calculate the imbalance and predict the pressure on price.

transcript.text: International Trade: Quotas
GENERAL ECONOMICS
GEN-ECON-25
Time: 5 minutes
Outcome: Analyze International Trade: Quotas.
Difficulty: Beginner
THE CORE IDEA

An import quota directly limits the quantity of a good that may enter the country. A binding quota reduces imports below their free-trade level, raises the domestic price, increases domestic production, and reduces domestic consumption. The price gap between the domestic quota price and the world price creates quota rent. Who receives that rent affects the country's national-surplus result, while the production and consumption distortions create deadweight loss.
HOW TO RECOGNIZE IT
Begin with the free-trade outcome at the world price.
A binding import quota limits imports below their free-trade quantity.
The restriction raises domestic price, increases domestic production, and reduces domestic consumption.
The gap between the quota price and world price creates quota rent on each permitted import.
Look for deadweight loss from excessive domestic production and reduced consumption.
WATCH OUT

Do not assume quota rent automatically becomes government revenue. It accrues to whoever holds the import rights; auctioning those rights can transfer the rent to government. The recipient matters for national welfare, while production and consumption distortions create deadweight loss.
WORKED EXAMPLE: QUOTA PRICE AND IMPORTS

The horizontal axis is quantity of phone cases and the vertical axis is their price in dollars. Quantity is measured in thousands as printed on the axis. Domestic demand slopes down and domestic supply slopes up, crossing at price $7 and quantity 175 thousand. Horizontal lines mark world price $3 and domestic price under quota $6. At $3, supply is 75 thousand and demand is 275 thousand; at $6, supply is 150 thousand and demand is 200 thousand.

Before trade, domestic supply and demand intersect at a price of $7. With free trade, buyers can purchase at the $3 world price, which creates imports. The quota limits imports, so the domestic price rises to $6. The difference between the $6 quota price and the $3 world price is $3 per imported unit; that $3 gap is quota rent.
CHECK YOURSELF
World price is $3 and the quota raises domestic price to $6. What is the rent per imported unit, and why does the identity of the license holder matter for national surplus?
